data.title: Stars walk blue carpet under hot sun ahead of TV's Emmy Awards
data.description:
* Stars of television walk blue carpet

* More than 27,000 Television Academy members choose winners

* Late-night variety category could produce multiple winners

(Recasts with stars arriving, paragraphs 1-4)

By Lisa Richwine and Danielle Broadway

LOS ANGELES, Sept 14 (Reuters) - Noah Wyle, Selena Gomez and other television luminaries gathered on Monday at the Primetime Emmy Awards, where "The Pitt" was seeking to repeat as best drama and Jean Smart and Harrison Ford were pursuing milestone victories of their own.

Celebrities walked a blue carpet, chosen by broadcaster NBC in place of the traditional red, leading into the Peacock Theater in downtown Los Angeles on an unusually warm afternoon before the ceremony to honor the best of television.

"It's the surface of the sun out here," joked "Nobody Wants This" star Kristen Bell, adding "there's a lot of friendship in the air" and a "familial vibe."

"Hacks" actor and nominee Meg Stalter stood out in an all-gold outfit that mirrored the Emmy statuette. She wore giant wings and held a large gold globe above her head as she posed for photographs.

Mariska Hargitay, star of NBC's drama "Law & Order: Special Victims ​Unit," will host the ceremony, breaking with a tradition of having a comedian serve as emcee. The festivities will be broadcast ​live at 8 p.m. ET (0000 GMT on Tuesday) on NBC and stream on Peacock. Presenters will include Sally Field, Jon Hamm, Amy Poehler and Zendaya.

TINSELTOWN ON EDGE

The Emmys offered a rare night of celebration as Hollywood grapples with production cutbacks, anxiety over artificial intelligence and the proposed Paramount Skydance ( PSKY ) purchase of HBO owner Warner Bros Discovery ( WBD ), a deal that has divided the industry and faces legal challenges.

"Hacks" star Smart could become the first performer to win the Emmy for best comedy actress in every season of a TV show's run while Ford could claim his first Emmy at age 84 for "Shrinking."

HBO Max's "The Pitt," set in a Pittsburgh trauma center, is favored to win best drama - the night's top award - for a second straight year. Competitors include newcomer "Pluribus," an Apple TV show about a woman at war with an alien hive mind. "The Pitt" star Wyle is a leading contender for a second straight best actor Emmy.

"Hacks," featuring Smart as a septuagenarian stand-up comic fighting to stay relevant, looked like the clear frontrunner two months ago. Also on HBO Max, the series earned best comedy once in its previous four seasons.

The show must fend off surging support, however, for Apple TV's "Widow's Bay," a new horror comedy starring Matthew Rhys as mayor of a small New England town that appears to be cursed.

Emmy winners are chosen by the more than 27,000 writers, directors, performers, producers and craftspeople in the Television Academy.

This year, the academy revamped the late-night comedy competition. Shows including "The Late Show with Stephen Colbert," which was canceled by CBS, and ABC's "Jimmy Kimmel Live" will compete for outstanding variety series in a category that could produce more than one winner. Under the academy's rules, each nominee is judged individually and any show with 90% approval receives an Emmy.

(Reporting by Lisa Richwine and Danielle Broadway; Additional reporting by Matt Silverstein; Editing by Alistair Bell and Howard Goller)

data.title: Costco Wholesale Nearly Doubles Kirkland Motor Oil Price, Caps Purchases at Two Weekly
data.description:
07:40 PM EDT, 09/14/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Costco Wholesale ( COST ) has raised prices on its Kirkland Signature private-label motor oil and imposed weekly purchase limits as crude oil prices continue to climb, the multiple outlets reported Monday.

Costco's Kirkland Signature full-synthetic motor oil 5-quart two-pack now costs around $58, up from about $30 last year, and purchases are limited to two boxes per week, according to the reports.

The retailer is also limiting purchases of Mobil 1's full-synthetic 1-quart six-pack, priced at about $44, to five per membership, the reports said.

Costco did not immediately respond to MT Newswires' request for comment.

data.title: Canada Pitches Itself As Safe Investment Destination
data.description:
07:11 PM EDT, 09/14/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Canada is a safe place to invest in an "uncertain world," Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne told AFP on Monday, ahead of the Canada Investment Summit.

Prime Minister Mark Carney is using the summit to encourage global business leaders to invest in Canada as the country seeks to diversify its economy and reduce its reliance on the US, AFP reported.

Major US investors, including representatives from Bank of America and Berkshire Hathaway, are expected to attend, along with Nigerian businessman Aliko Dangote and Gulf investment agencies, the report said.

Champagne told AFP that attendees control more than CA$120 trillion ($86 trillion) in global capital. He said the government understands that speed and skill are needed to capitalize on the opportunity, the report said.

data.title: Trump Dismisses AI Risk as "Hoax" During Live Call With Nvidia's Huang
data.description:
07:16 PM EDT, 09/14/2026 (MT Newswires) -- President Donald Trump said concerns about artificial intelligence are "all a hoax" and that data centers "make people wealthy, and they make states wealthy," during a call with Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang, who put him on speakerphone while speaking on stage at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles Monday, CNBC reported, citing a video posted by an attendee.

Trump also called data centers the "oil of the next 20, 25 years" and told Huang, "I'm with you all the way," according to the report.

Trump has published multiple posts describing AI safety concerns as a "hoax" and a "scam," including one calling those worried about AI and data centers "Revolutionaries for a Bad and Evil Cause," and said he sees no need for additional AI regulation.
